newsitem.title: USA: Telmex to target US long distance market.
newsitem.headline: Telmex to target US long distance market.

text.p: Mexican telecommunications company Telefonos de Mexico SA would like to enter the U.S. long-distance market by targeting the growing hispanic population, a senior company executive said on Tuesday.

Telmex sees "an outstanding opportunity to expand into the U.S. market at the same time the Mexican market is opening," chief financial officer Adolfo Cerezo told a telecommunications conference sponsored by Salomon Brothers.
He said an effort to enter the U.S. long-distance market could be done through Telmex's alliance with Sprint Corp.
About 90 percent of Mexico's international calls now go to the United States.
Telmex would rely on its high name recognition among hispanics, "stronger in many cases than the names of U.S. company's," he said.
"This is not a niche market. This is really a huge marget segment in the U.S.," he said. "We would rely on our alliance with Sprint and that means long-distance."

Carlos Casasus, president of Mexico's Federal Telecommunications Commission, said the new U.S. telecommunications law opening up long-distance competition removed a snag from Telmex's entry into the United States.

SBC Communications Inc Inc, along with France Telecom, is a major partner in Telmex. As a former Baby Bell company, SBC had been barred until passage of the law this year from participating in long-distance service.
"Basically Telmex should be able to get a license from the Federal Communications Commission to provide long-distance service with Sprint in the United States, " he said.
"I believe that Telmex is capable of coming to the U.S. and competing successfully."
